decision_description: Resolves the single flagged item left open by the phase 2 scope check recorded in docs/tier4_orchestration_state/decision_log/topic-scope-check_d68acaef.json. That check loaded only scope_requirements.json and call_constraints.json and flagged concept claim C22 (the work package holds an open place for the Joint Research Centre as a zero-funding beneficiary or associated partner) as not covered by any loaded Tier 2B scope element or constraint, with resolution_status unresolved. Review of Tier 2B eligibility_conditions.json confirms EC-02 addresses JRC participation directly: the Joint Research Centre may participate as a member of the selected consortium as a beneficiary with zero funding, or as an associated partner, and does not participate in preparation and submission. C22 is therefore in-scope and grounded in Tier 2B. The flag arose from an incomplete file set at scope-check time, not from an absent or conflicting source. With this resolution the concept_refinement_summary scope_conflict_log is empty, satisfying the phase 2 gate condition that no unresolved scope conflicts remain.
alternatives_considered: Drop claim C22 from the concept to remove the flagged item. Rejected: EC-02 shows JRC participation is a named call-level eligibility exception, so the claim is admissible and removing it would discard a topic-supported provision.

Leave the item unresolved and carry it forward. Rejected: the phase 2 gate condition requires no unresolved scope conflicts, and CLAUDE.md 12.3 requires explicit resolution rather than deferral once the governing source is identified.
rationale: The prior scope check evaluated C22 against only two of the Tier 2B extracted files and could not confirm it, so it flagged the claim rather than asserting it, per CLAUDE.md 13.2. The correct authority for JRC participation is the eligibility condition set, not scope_requirements.json or call_constraints.json. EC-02 (traceable to work programme page 73, source SRC-WP9-P73) names the JRC open place as a topic-level eligibility exception, which grounds C22 in Tier 2B and removes the flag. Recording the resolution here, naming the governing file, keeps the decision durable and reviewable under CLAUDE.md 9.4 rather than resting only in agent memory.
